decisions.rationale: Lead Alolan Ninetales and Whimsicott to replace opposing sun with snow, establish Aurora Veil or Prankster Tailwind, and enable accurate Blizzard. Mega Blastoise is the primary special attacker, while Tauros-Blaze supplies Intimidate, Rock Slide pressure on Charizard, and strong Fighting coverage into Excadrill.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 selection: Ninetales-Alola + Whimsicott lead, Mega Blastoise + Tauros-Paldea-Blaze in back. Core plan is to overwrite Drought with snow, use Veil/Tailwind support, then attack with Mega Blastoise and Tauros. Gholdengo and Maushold remain available as alternate compositions in later games.

decisions.rationale: Lead Charizard+Venusaur: Mega Y Drought sets sun, Chlorophyll Venusaur becomes speed demon. Bench Rotom-Wash pivots with Volt Switch and covers Water, Excadrill Mold Breaker handles Gholdengo and sets hazards.
decisions.notebook: Sun team core: Mega Charizard Y Drought + Chlorophyll Venusaur. Opponent Fairy-types weak to Fire under sun. Rotom-Wash for pivoting/coverage, Excadrill for Mold Breaker Earthquake/hazards. Toxapex and Weavile remain hidden options. Series 0-0, game 1.

decisions.rationale: Switch Ninetales to Blastoise to avoid the likely sun-boosted Fire attack while preserving the Mega option. Whimsicott sets Tailwind first with Prankster, giving the backline speed control and enabling Blastoise and Tauros to pressure the opposing core next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 plan: prioritize preserving the Ninetales/Blastoise/Tauros weather-and-offense core; Tailwind is the preferred opening speed control. Gholdengo and Maushold remain available as alternate compositions in later games.

decisions.rationale: Mega Charizard Y sets Drought (replaces Snowscape), Fire Blast OHKO's Ninetales-Alola (2x, ~110-200% under sun). Venusaur Sludge Bomb OHKO's Whimsicott (4x, ~160-314%). Double KO removes both revealed foes, eliminates hail, and establishes sun for Chlorophyll Venusaur going forward.
decisions.notebook: Sun team core: Mega Charizard Y Drought + Chlorophyll Venusaur. Opponent Fairy-types weak to Fire under sun. Need to track hidden options: Blastoise, Gholdengo, Tauros-Paldea-Blaze, Maushold. Rotom-Wash and Excadrill still benched for pivoting/hazards. Series 0-0, game 1 turn 1.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolve Blastoise and use Helping Hand to maximize Water Pulse into Charizard. Whimsicott is already at 1% and will likely be removed by Charizard or Venusaur, but its priority Helping Hand still amplifies Blastoise’s attack before fainting.
decisions.notebook: Tailwind is established in Game 1. Preserve the Ninetales-Alola/Blastoise/Tauros-Paldea-Blaze weather-and-offense core when possible. Gholdengo and Maushold remain available as alternate compositions for later games.

decisions.rationale: Switch to Ninetales-Alola to replace sun with snow, suppress Venusaur's Chlorophyll speed boost, and disrupt SolarBeam while preserving the weather-and-offense core. Blastoise should remain in play rather than concede.
decisions.notebook: Tailwind is established in Game 1. Opponent's revealed Charizard-Mega-Y and Venusaur form a sun/Chlorophyll core; replacing sun with snow is a valuable disruption. Preserve the Ninetales-Alola/Blastoise/Tauros-Paldea-Blaze weather-and-offense core when possible. Gholdengo and Maushold remain available as alternate compositions for later games.

decisions.rationale: Air Slash at 95% accuracy reliably KOes Whimsicott at 1% HP (Flying is 2x super effective) while avoiding Fire Blast's 85% miss risk that could let Whimsicott Encore or set up. Giga Drain hits Blastoise super effectively (Grass vs Water) and heals Venusaur, maintaining longevity against a dangerous Ice Beam threat.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Tailwind 3 turns remaining. Blastoise carries Blastoisinite - may Mega Evolve, watch for Mega Launcher-boosted AuraSphere/WaterPulse. Ninetales-Alola, Gholdengo, Tauros-Paldea-Blaze, Maushold still hidden options. Rotom-Wash and Excadrill remain in reserve for pivoting and hazard control. Sun team core: Mega Charizard Y Drought + Chlorophyll Venusaur. Fairy-types weak to Fire under sun. Prioritize removing Whimsicott setup potential then apply offensive pressure.

decisions.rationale: Switch Blastoise to preserve it from likely Venusaur pressure while bringing Tauros in safely; Ninetales uses Blizzard to threaten both foes and guarantee the shown low-HP Charizard KO if it connects. Snow and Tailwind support the offensive sequence.
decisions.notebook: Opponent revealed a Charizard-Mega-Y/Venusaur sun-Chlorophyll core, with Rotom-Wash, Toxapex, Excadrill, and Weavile as possible alternatives. Snow disruption is valuable. Preserve the Ninetales-Alola/Blastoise-Mega/Tauros-Paldea-Blaze weather-offense core when practical. Gholdengo and Maushold remain available as alternate compositions for later games.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Ninetales-Alola is the biggest threat: fastest Pokémon with Tailwind, can set Aurora Veil to cripple our damage, and has Blizzard for Venusaur. Both Fire Blast and Sludge Bomb are 2x super effective into it. Combined damage should threaten a KO even through Aurora Veil. Removing Ninetales also kills Snowscape sustainability and lets us clean up 24% Blastoise next turn.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Tailwind 2 turns left. Snowscape active 5 turns. Blastoise-Mega at 24% HP with Blastoisinite. Ninetales-Alola is primary win-con threat via Aurora Veil + Blizzard spread. Sun team core (Drought + Chlorophyll) neutralized by Snowscape. Prioritize removing Ninetales then finish Blastoise. Keep Rotom-Wash and Excadrill in reserve for pivoting and hazard control.

decisions.rationale: Switch Rotom-Wash into slot a to threaten Tauros with super effective Hydro Pump next turn despite Tailwind speed disadvantage; Venusaur passes as it's at 42% with -1 Atk and no favorable matchup. Rotom-Wash's Levitate provides Ground immunity and Volt Switch offers future pivoting.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Tailwind 2 turns left. Snowscape 5 turns. Blastoise-Mega at 24% HP with Blastoisinite is weakened—eliminate after handling Tauros. Ninetales-Alola win-con is dead. Preserve Excadrill for hazard control and late-game cleaning. Sun core (Drought+Chlorophyll) remains neutralized by Snowscape. Rotom-Wash is the primary Water-type attacker for the Tauros matchup.

decisions.rationale: Both foes can KO either weakened Pokémon, so protecting only one leaves the other exposed. Double-targeting Rotom gives the best chance to remove its immediate Hydro Pump/Thunderbolt threat before it acts: Close Combat may finish it, while Mega Launcher-boosted Aura Sphere adds substantial damage. Venusaur is then the remaining target.
decisions.notebook: Opponent favors a sun-Chlorophyll core with Charizard/Venusaur; weather disruption is valuable. Preserve the Ninetales-Alola, Mega Blastoise, and Tauros-Paldea-Blaze weather-offense core when practical. Gholdengo and Maushold remain available as alternate compositions for future games.

decisions.rationale: Hydro Pump on Tauros threatens OHKO (80-189% damage range, 2x super effective) on the biggest immediate threat. Giga Drain on Blastoise-Mega guarantees KO (Blastoise at 24% HP, minimum Giga Drain damage is 43% of max) while recovering HP for Venusaur. Eliminating both active foes wins the game; even eliminating just Blastoise leaves Excadrill to clean up a weakened Tauros next turn.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Tailwind 2 turns left. Snowscape active. Blastoise-Mega at 24% HP with Blastoisinite is a priority elimination target. Ninetales-Alola win-con is dead. Preserve Excadrill for hazard control and late-game cleaning. Sun core (Drought+Chlorophyll) neutralized by Snowscape. Rotom-Wash is primary Water attacker for Tauros matchup. After this turn, if Blastoise is eliminated and Tauros is chipped, Excadrill Earthquake becomes the finisher.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Tauros outspeeds both foes and Flare Blitz guarantees the KO on Venusaur before it can act. Blastoise targets Excadrill with super-effective Water Pulse; even with Focus Sash, this maximizes pressure on the remaining threat while avoiding leaving Venusaur active.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s preferred structure is a sun-Chlorophyll Charizard/Venusaur core; weather disruption is valuable. Preserve the Ninetales-Alola, Mega Blastoise, and Tauros-Paldea-Blaze weather-offense core when practical. Gholdengo and Maushold remain available as alternate compositions for future games.

decisions.rationale: Focus fire on priority target Blastoise-Mega (24% HP). Venusaur's Giga Drain is 2x super-effective and heals Venusaur; Excadrill's Rapid Spin adds neutral damage to help secure the KO. Once Blastoise is eliminated, Excadrill's Focus Sash lets it survive Tauros's hit next turn and Earthquake clean up.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Tailwind 2 turns left. Snowscape active 3 turns. Preserve Excadrill for hazard control and late-game cleaning. Sun core neutralized. After Blastoise elimination and Tauros chip, Excadrill Earthquake becomes finisher. Rotom-Wash remains dead. Ninetales-Alola win-con dead.

decisions.rationale: Tauros protects against Excadrill’s faster attack while Mega Blastoise uses Water Pulse to finish the 1% Excadrill. This preserves Tauros and avoids risking both Pokémon to a likely Earthquake.
decisions.notebook: Opponent favors a sun-Chlorophyll Charizard/Venusaur core; weather disruption is valuable. Preserve the Ninetales-Alola, Mega Blastoise, and Tauros-Paldea-Blaze weather-offense core when practical. Gholdengo and Maushold remain available as alternate compositions for future games.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill Earthquake hits both foes; 2x vs Tauros and neutral vs Blastoise, both low HP. Excadrill's 220 Speed guarantees it moves first, potentially cleaning the entire field. Any other move risks leaving a foe alive to KO Excadrill at 1%.

Close Combat is guaranteed to hit and is super effective against the 1% Excadrill, securing the knockout despite Excadrill moving first. Protect is unreliable after last turn’s use, while Rock Slide is resisted. Blastoise has no action.
decisions.notebook: Opponent favors sun-Chlorophyll Charizard/Venusaur cores; weather disruption remains valuable. Preserve the Ninetales-Alola, Mega Blastoise, and Tauros-Paldea-Blaze weather-offense core when practical. Gholdengo and Maushold remain available as alternate compositions for future games.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill is faster (220 vs 132-167) and Earthquake guarantees a KO on Tauros at 15% HP (75.8-169.3% damage range). Even though Tauros's retaliatory Close Combat/Flare Blitz/Rock Slide will KO Excadrill in return, Excadrill's Earthquake resolves first and eliminates the opponent's last Pokémon, winning the game. Venusaur is fainted so must pass.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's last conscious Pokémon is Tauros-Paldea-Blaze at 15% HP with -1/-1 defenses. My only conscious Pokémon is Excadrill at 1% HP with +1 Speed. Focus Sash already consumed. Earthquake is the strongest and most reliable finishing move. Preserve hazard control for potential future games. Sun core and Ninetales-Alola win-con are dead for this game.

reflections.summary: Lost mainly because the preview plan lacked a reliable endgame into Excadrill: Mega Blastoise was a poor Mega choice into Venusaur plus Earthquake pressure, and the final Protect let Excadrill survive while Earthquake removed the unprotected partner. The weather core did answer Charizard/Venusaur, but the four brought did not cover the follow-up well.
reflections.adjustment: Change the four and consider not centering the matchup on Mega Blastoise; include an available option that pressures or safely handles Excadrill. If using this core again, when Excadrill is at risk of being KOed, attack it with Tauros while Protecting Blastoise rather than Protecting Tauros.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's sun mode is confirmed as Charizard-Y/Venusaur, with Excadrill as a Sash-based Mold Breaker follow-up using Rapid Spin, Earthquake, and a Speed boost; Rotom-Wash supports the mode. Weather disruption remains valuable, but future previews must include a dedicated Excadrill plan. Mega Blastoise is vulnerable to this combination and should not be an automatic Mega choice; consider a Gholdengo- or Maushold-based alternative composition when it improves the Excadrill matchup.

reflections.summary: Opponent's Sun + Snow dual-weather team was dismantled because our Venusaur correctly walled their Sun core and eliminated both Whimsicott and Ninetales-Alola, stripping their weather strategies. Excadrill on Focus Sash survived Tauros-Paldea-Blaze's Intimidate drops and delivered the finishing Earthquakes after Blastoise-Mega fell. The opponent's wincon narrowed entirely to Tauros once their weather core died, and Excadrill's Mold Breaker ignored the Speed drops to clean up.
reflections.adjustment: Rotom-Wash contributed almost nothing before being random-crit fainted by Tauros's Close Combat on Turn 4. Consider replacing it with a faster Tauros check or a Pokémon that can threaten Ninetales-Alola directly (e.g., a Fighting or Rock type), so the midgame doesn't rely on a 55% Speed tier pivot surviving a Life Orb critical hit.
reflections.notebook: Opponent runs dual-weather: Sun core (Whimsicott Tailwind + Charizard-Mega-Y Drought) backed by Ninetales-Alola Snowscape as backup. Tauros-Paldea-Blaze (Intimidate / Life Orb) is primary wincon and late-game cleaner. Blastoise-Mega is their mid-game special wall. Gholdengo and Maushold are unused bench options — expect potential surprise picks in future games. Whimsicott carries Focus Sash to guarantee Tailwind setup. Opponent's Snow team threatens our Charizard and Fire types heavily. Next game: plan for Gholdengo or Maushold appearing; consider whether Rotom-Wash slot should be a dedicated Tauros/Ninetales answer.
